text:
Alex: FYI — AcmeMaps (tenant_id: acme-34) opened a Sev2. Intermittent 429s during short ingestion bursts. They say spikes are very short (4–8s) but big: ~1.2k rps peak. Happening across multiple routes (generate & batch-embed).
Alex: root log snippet from 15:42:10 UTC:
```
[2025-11-14T15:42:11Z] req_id=01EEXAMPLE status=429 route=/v1/generate headers={"X-RateLimit-Limit":"18000/min","X-RateLimit-Remaining":"0","X-RateLimit-Reset":"26","X-Redwood-Burst-Credits":"0"} latency_ms=48
```
Alex: attached their curl repro (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key-acme>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"map-v1","prompt":"...","max_tokens":64}'
```
Alex: We think burst credits drained. They rely on short spikes, not sustained traffic. Can infra/eng confirm our burst handling behavior and any fast mitigation? cc @Priya @Sam @Marta :thinking_face:

Priya: Thanks Alex. Can you drop one example request-id (from logs) + the exact timestamp window? Also, does the customer use client-side retry/backoff? Short spikes often require smoothing client-side even with burst credits.

Alex: Pasted req_id above (01EEXAMPLE) and window ~15:42:08–15:42:18. Customer says they have naive immediate retries (no jitter).

Sam: I looked at the infra traces. Short summary: our limiter = per-tenant token-bucket + global burst-credit pool. Design notes: token refill = quota/60 per second; burst pool = tenant_burst_factor * quota (default tenant_burst_factor=0.5) as short-term credit. Behavior we saw: when incoming rate > quota + burst for > ~10–15s the burst pool hits 0 and we start returning 429s. In this case the customer hit ~3x quota briefly — burst drained around 15:42:11 and stayed at 0 for ~27s.

Sam: Quick console check (internal command):
```
infra-cli tenant burst-status acme-34
# output
tenant: acme-34
quota: 18000/min
burst_pool_capacity: 9000 (50%)
burst_pool_remaining: 0
last_refill: 2025-11-14T15:42:38Z
```
Sam: So we behaved as-configured. Short spikes should be absorbed if they fit within burst_pool_capacity and the spike duration is short (<~10s). Their burst exceeded what burst pool could cover.

Priya: Two immediate mitigation paths: 1) short-term: give a temporary burst top-up / quota bump (billing approve), 2) longer-term: recommend client smoothing + server-side route smoothing (we have a smoothing policy for per-route rolling-window averaging). Also ask customer to add full-jitter backoff and concurrency cap — spikes often come from concurrent clients doing fan-out.

Priya: Example client advice (python asyncio token-bucket + jitter):
```
# naive example
import asyncio, time, random
class TokenBucket:
  def __init__(self, rate, capacity):
    self.rate = rate
    self.capacity = capacity
    self.tokens = capacity
    self.last = time.monotonic()
  async def consume(self, n=1):
    while True:
      now = time.monotonic()
      self.tokens = min(self.capacity, self.tokens + (now-self.last)*self.rate)
      self.last = now
      if self.tokens >= n:
        self.tokens -= n
        return
      await asyncio.sleep(0.01 + random.random()*0.02)
# add exponential backoff with full jitter on 429s
```

Marta: Billing notes — if we bump quota or add one-time burst credits we should log it as a one-off credit (no auto-downgrade). Also warn the customer that repeated overages will be billed per contract. I'm OK with a single 24h temporary top-up to unblock them. I'll draft a credit offer.

ratebot: automated metric snapshot for acme-34 (15:41:30–15:43:00):
```
{"tenant":"acme-34","p95_rps":1020,"p99_rps":1210,"burst_credits_used":9000,"burst_credits_capacity":9000,"429_count":312}
```

Sam: follow-up technical points:
- Our bucket implementation allows short bursts up to burst_pool_capacity, but refill window is per-second; extremely sharp spikes can cause headroom to be insufficient.
- We have two knobs: tenant_burst_factor and route_smoothing_window. Increasing tenant_burst_factor increases short-term absorbable bursts but raises risk of resource contention.
- We also have a per-tenant concurrency cap (default 200). If the customer hits concurrency limits, their client-side fan-out may need a cap.

Alex: Customer asks: "Can you automatically smooth bursts on our account so we don't hit 429s for short spikes?" What's safe to promise?

Priya: For hosted customers, we can do the following (non-breaking):
- Apply a one-time burst credit top-up (Marta to approve) that refills their burst pool immediately.
- Enable route-level smoothing with a 10s rolling average that will reduce instantaneous token consumption by smoothing short bursts (this introduced latency tradeoff of ~5–20ms on average but prevents 429 spiky behavior).
- If they need guaranteed headroom for spikes, recommend Dedicated capacity or reserved throughput plan.

Marta: I'll offer a 24h burst top-up equal to 100% of their burst_pool_capacity (9000 credits) and a temporary +25% quota bump for 48h. I'll include notes about billing if they continue to exceed.

Sam: Action items:
- Priya: check whether we can safely increase tenant_burst_factor to 0.75 for acme-34 temporarily (risks: increased tail load). ETA 2h.
- Alex: send the customer the recommended client changes (token bucket + full jitter + concurrency cap) + temporary creds update when Marta confirms.
- Marta: draft & send the credit offer to AcmeMaps; please include tracking code and ticket ID.
- Sam: enable additional monitoring alert on burst_pool_remaining < 20% for that tenant for the next 72h.

Alex: I'll message the customer now and paste these mitigations. If anyone sees further anomalies in the next hour ping here. :thumbsup:
